lead.headline: CYCLONE ARNAB DAMAGE SPREADS ACROSS ANDHRA; NINE REPORTED DEAD
lead.deck: Preliminary estimates put crop damage at 2.24 lakh hectares, affecting 3.45 lakh farmers

image.alt: Cyclone Arnab battering the Andhra Pradesh coast
image.caption: Arnab made landfall Wednesday and weakened as it moved inland. (Representative image / ANI)

paragraphs: Cyclone Arnab’s passage across Andhra Pradesh has left nine people dead, according to a report published early Thursday. The storm made landfall Wednesday and weakened as it moved inland.

Preliminary state estimates put crop damage at 2.24 lakh hectares across 14 districts, with nearly 3.45 lakh farmers affected. Paddy fields were among the hardest hit, while officials reported damage to homes and infrastructure.
The India Meteorological Department expects the system to move north-northwest and weaken gradually over the next 48 hours. Relief and damage assessments are continuing.

sidebarStory.headline: BENGALURU DOUBLE-DECKER METRO PLAN SHELVED
sidebarStory.subhead: BMRCL has dropped the proposed 44.65-km project after it failed to secure Union approval
paragraphs: Bengaluru Metro Rail Corporation Limited has permanently shelved its proposed double-decker infrastructure project, which was planned across 44.65 km, after the proposal failed to secure Union government approval.

stories.headline: NDA SWEEPS ALL FOUR KARNATAKA COUNCIL SEATS
stories.subhead: JD(S) wrests Bengaluru Teachers’ constituency as Congress loses every contest
paragraphs: The BJP-led NDA won all four Karnataka Legislative Council seats contested on October 23. The BJP retained three constituencies while JD(S) took Bengaluru Teachers’, defeating incumbent Congress MLC Puttanna by 908 votes.
The result is a setback for the ruling Congress among teachers and graduates, though it does not change the party’s majority in the 75-member council.

stories.headline: BENGALURU DOUBLE-DECKER METRO PLAN SHELVED
stories.subhead: The 44.65-km proposal failed to obtain Union government approval
paragraphs: BMRCL has shelved its proposed double-decker infrastructure project covering 44.65 km across Bengaluru after the plan failed to secure approval from the Union government.

stories.headline: KARNATAKA SHIFTS 87 ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICE OFFICERS
paragraphs: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar ordered transfers of 87 KAS officers, including nine postings as assistant commissioners and four as additional deputy commissioners. Twenty-eight officers are assigned to the Urban Development and Rural Development departments.

stories.headline: ARNAB LEAVES NINE DEAD; CROPS DAMAGED ACROSS 2.24 LAKH HECTARES
stories.deck: Nearly 3.45 lakh farmers are affected across 14 districts, preliminary estimates indicate

image.alt: Cyclone Arnab bringing heavy rain to Andhra Pradesh
image.caption: The cyclone made landfall Wednesday and weakened as it moved inland. (ANI / Moneycontrol)

paragraphs: Cyclone Arnab left nine people dead along Andhra Pradesh’s coast, according to a report published early Thursday. The system made landfall Wednesday and the IMD expects it to weaken gradually.
Preliminary estimates put crop damage at 2.24 lakh hectares in 14 districts, affecting nearly 3.45 lakh farmers. The state has sought central support as relief and damage assessments continue.

stories.headline: CABINET APPROVES 3% DEARNESS ALLOWANCE HIKE
paragraphs: The Union Cabinet approved a three-percentage-point increase in dearness allowance for central government employees and dearness relief for pensioners, effective July 1. The increase takes DA to 63% of basic pay and benefits about 11.6 million people.

stories.headline: NDA TAKES 16 OF 28 COUNCIL SEATS ACROSS FOUR STATES
paragraphs: The BJP-led NDA won 16 of 28 Legislative Council seats contested across four states. The results included a sweep of all four Karnataka seats, while Bihar and Maharashtra returned split verdicts.

stories.headline: BENGALURU’S 44.65-KM DOUBLE-DECKER METRO PLAN SCRAPPED
stories.deck: BMRCL shelved the proposal after it failed to receive Union government approval
paragraphs: Bengaluru Metro Rail Corporation Limited has permanently shelved its proposed double-decker infrastructure project, which was planned across 44.65 km of the city. The plan failed to secure Union government approval.
The decision ends a long-proposed effort to combine Metro and road infrastructure on elevated corridors.

stories.headline: 87 KAS OFFICERS TRANSFERRED; 28 POSTED TO TWO DEPARTMENTS
paragraphs: The reshuffle assigns 15 officers to Urban Development and 13 to Rural Development and Panchayat Raj, with nine posted as assistant commissioners.

stories.headline: 716 FOREIGN NATIONALS REMOVED FROM KARNATAKA VOTER ROLLS
paragraphs: Election officials said document verification during the Special Intensive Revision identified 716 ineligible entries linked to foreign nationals. Bengaluru North accounted for 583 of the removals.

stories.headline: NDA’S KARNATAKA SWEEP DEALS CONGRESS A COUNCIL POLL SETBACK
stories.deck: BJP retains three seats and JD(S) takes Bengaluru Teachers’ constituency

image.caption: The NDA won all four Karnataka Legislative Council seats contested this week.

paragraphs: The BJP-led NDA swept all four Karnataka Legislative Council seats, with BJP retaining three and JD(S) wresting Bengaluru Teachers’ from Congress. JD(S) candidate A.P. Ranganath defeated incumbent Puttanna by 908 votes.
The result gives the opposition alliance momentum among the state’s teachers and graduates constituencies.
